domain.name: Project Management & Operations
domain.description: Practical scoping, scheduling, risk, SOPs, capacity, quality, vendor coordination, and continuous improvement.

competencies.name: Scope & Work Breakdown
competencies.description: Turn a desired outcome into bounded deliverables and executable work.
competencies.purpose: Prevent vague projects from becoming uncontrolled effort.

units.title: Scope defines both included and excluded work
units.content: A useful scope states outcomes, deliverables, assumptions, constraints, responsibilities, and exclusions so change can be recognized instead of silently absorbed.

units.title: Work breakdown workflow
units.content: Define the final outcome; identify major deliverables; break them into manageable work packages; assign acceptance criteria; surface dependencies and owner responsibilities; then estimate effort.

units.title: Scope failures
units.content: Avoid vague deliverables, hidden assumptions, tasks with no owner, and adding work without recording the effect on time, cost, or quality.

drills.title: Break down a website project
drills.prompt: Create a work breakdown for a service-business website from discovery through launch.

competencies.name: Scheduling & Dependencies
competencies.description: Sequence work according to prerequisites, timing, and resource reality.
competencies.purpose: Create schedules that reflect how work actually flows.

units.title: Dependencies create the real schedule
units.content: A date list is not a schedule unless it accounts for prerequisites, review time, handoffs, resource constraints, and uncertainty.

units.title: Dependency-based scheduling
units.content: List work packages; identify hard and soft dependencies; estimate duration and review lag; mark critical sequencing; assign owners; add buffers where uncertainty is meaningful; then update with actual progress.

units.title: Scheduling failures
units.content: Avoid planning every task in parallel, forgetting client approvals, treating estimates as commitments, and hiding delays until the final deadline.

drills.title: Build an event-production schedule
drills.prompt: Sequence preproduction, gear prep, capture, backup, edit, review, revision, and delivery for a client event.

competencies.name: Risk & Issue Management
competencies.description: Identify uncertainty early and respond to problems with ownership and mitigation.

units.title: Risks are future possibilities; issues are current problems
units.content: Risks need probability, impact, trigger, and mitigation; issues need owner, action, priority, and resolution tracking.

units.title: Risk review
units.content: List material risks; rate likelihood and impact; define prevention, contingency, trigger, and owner; review at milestones; convert realized risks into tracked issues.

units.title: Risk failures
units.content: Avoid giant risk lists with no priorities, vague owners, mitigation that begins after the trigger, and calling known current problems risks.

drills.title: Build a launch risk register
drills.prompt: Create a concise risk register for launching a client web app with external integrations and a fixed date.

competencies.name: SOPs & Process Mapping
competencies.description: Document repeatable work clearly enough that another capable person can execute it.
competencies.purpose: Create consistency and reduce dependence on memory.

units.title: Build an SOP from real work
units.content: Observe the current process; define trigger and outcome; map steps, decisions, inputs, tools, exceptions, and quality checks; test with another person; revise from execution feedback.

units.title: Document decisions, not only clicks
units.content: An SOP should explain when paths change and what good looks like, not merely list mechanical steps.

units.title: SOP failures
units.content: Avoid documentation that assumes hidden knowledge, screenshots with no decision logic, no owner, no version/date, and processes never tested by a second operator.

drills.title: Write a gallery delivery SOP
drills.prompt: Document a client gallery workflow from ingest and backup through culling, editing, export, upload, QC, and delivery.

competencies.name: Capacity & Resource Planning
competencies.description: Match workload to available people, time, equipment, and constraints.

units.title: Capacity is usable throughput, not theoretical hours
units.content: Meetings, setup, switching, revisions, failures, and maintenance reduce the hours that can become completed work.

units.title: Capacity planning
units.content: Estimate available productive capacity; forecast committed demand; identify bottleneck skills or equipment; reserve buffer for variance; then decide what to accept, defer, outsource, or automate.

units.title: Capacity failures
units.content: Avoid booking 100 percent of theoretical time, assuming every worker is interchangeable, and measuring backlog only by task count instead of effort and priority.

drills.title: Plan weekly creative capacity
drills.prompt: Allocate editing capacity across three client projects with different deadlines, revision risk, and revenue importance.

competencies.name: Quality Assurance
competencies.description: Build checks that prevent defects from reaching the client or next stage.
competencies.purpose: Make quality repeatable instead of dependent on memory.

units.title: Quality is designed into the process
units.content: Inspection matters, but the strongest QA also reduces the chance of defects through standards, templates, automation, and clear acceptance criteria.

units.title: QA plan
units.content: Define critical quality attributes; identify failure points; add preventive controls and checkpoints; assign reviewer independence where needed; record defects; feed recurring failures back into the process.

units.title: QA failures
units.content: Avoid checking only at the end, relying on the creator's memory, treating every defect equally, and recording failures without changing the process.

drills.title: Design a video delivery QA checklist
drills.prompt: Create a QA process for final event-video delivery covering content, audio, color, titles, export settings, file integrity, and client requirements.

competencies.name: Vendor & Contractor Coordination
competencies.description: Coordinate external contributors with clear scope, access, timing, standards, and handoffs.

units.title: Contractor handoff brief
units.content: Define outcome, scope, files/access, standard, deadline, dependencies, communication channel, approval boundary, payment basis, and verification before work starts.

units.title: External capacity still needs internal ownership
units.content: Outsourcing work does not outsource accountability for scope, quality, security, or client communication.

units.title: Coordination failures
units.content: Avoid verbal-only scope, missing file conventions, unclear revision ownership, unverified delivery, and granting broader access than needed.

drills.title: Brief a freelance editor
drills.prompt: Create a contractor brief for editing a social campaign from supplied footage with fixed brand and delivery standards.

competencies.name: Retrospectives & Continuous Improvement
competencies.description: Turn project outcomes into durable process lessons.
competencies.purpose: Make repeated work get better instead of merely repeating.

units.title: Operational retrospective
units.content: Compare expected and actual outcome, time, cost, quality, and friction; identify what helped or hurt; distinguish one-off noise from recurring pattern; choose a small number of process changes; assign owner and verification.

units.title: Fix systems before blaming effort
units.content: When the same failure repeats across capable people, inspect process, information, tooling, incentives, and workload before concluding it is a motivation problem.

units.title: Retrospective failures
units.content: Avoid blame sessions, vague lessons like communicate better, dozens of action items, and improvements that are never checked later.

drills.title: Run a project retrospective
drills.prompt: A client project finished late but the final work was strong. Analyze schedule, scope, communication, rework, and process changes.
